q1: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2: WITH X AS (SELECT DISTINCT * FROM VIEWS) SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM X GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(VIEWER_ID ) >1 ORDER BY VIEWER_ID ASC
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2_prompt_sql: WITH X AS (SELECT DISTINCT * FROM VIEWS) SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM X GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(VIEWER_ID ) >1 ORDER BY VIEWER_ID ASC
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 groups by VIEW_DATE and VIEWER_ID, while Q2 groups by VIEW_DATE and VIEWER_ID after removing duplicates with a CTE. This difference in grouping can lead to different results, especially if there are multiple views on the same article by the same viewer on the same date.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have multiple views by the same viewer on the same date, and at least one view by a different viewer on the same date. The difference in results will be whether the viewer with multiple views is included in the output.
